newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Up to 15 years jail sought for Indonesia activists.
newsitem.headline: Up to 15 years jail sought for Indonesia activists.

text.p: Indonesian prosecutors on Monday sought jail sentences of between eight and 15 years for five left-wing political activists accused of subversion and spreading hatred against the government.

Budiman Sudjatmiko, chairman of the leftist People's Democratic Party (PRD), faces 15 years in jail, and Garda Sembiring, head of the affiliated Indonesia's Student Solidarity for Democracy (SMID), faces a jail sentence of 13 years.
"The defendant, Budiman Sudjatmiko, is guilty of subversion. We demand a jail sentence of 15 years," prosecutor M. Salim told the central Jakarta district court.
Prosecutors also sought sentences of eight to 10 years imprisonment for three other PRD activists accused of subversion and tried at the same court.
A date for judgement was not immediately set.
Sudjatmiko and Sembiring were tried separately at the court but their three other colleagues were tried together.
The five defendants had refused to enter the courtroom in protest against their trial. Subversion can be punished by death in Indonesia.

Sudjatmiko said in a statement distributed to reporters that he did not attend the proceedings because the prosecutors had failed to present competent witnesses. The statement gave no further details.
Most PRD leaders were arrested and charged with subversion after riots in Jakarta on July 27 last year that the government and military blamed on the group.

Prosecutors in Indonesia's second city of Surabaya last month sought jail sentences of six and eight years for two PRD activists on charges of manipulating, undermining and deviating from state policy guidelines.
The activists organised a major strike in Surabaya last July involving up to 20,000 workers.
The verdicts have not yet been handed down.
